title: Cardinal Billing Account Late-Payment Addition to the Installment Charge: Questions Answered
content:
**Rule.** A late-payment addition is added to the installment charge on a Cardinal Billing Account installment invoice: **$1.50** when two or more late fees were charged on the account in the last 12 whole months, **$0.75** when exactly one was, and none when none was. The addition is a dollar amount added to the relieved charge; it is not itself multiplied by any rate.

## Questions answered

**Which late fees count?**
Late fees charged on the account, as shown by the late fee entries on its billing history, posted less than 12 whole months before the invoice date, counted on calendar months. They count whichever term they belong to.

**Does a late fee that was later waived still count?**
Yes. The count is of late fees charged; a waiver is a separate entry and does not take the charge off the billing history.

| Late fees charged in the last 12 whole months | Addition |
|---|---|
| 0 | None |
| 1 | $0.75 |
| 2 or more | $1.50 |

**Hypothetical figure.** A relieved charge of $2.40 on an account with one late fee in the window becomes $3.15 with the addition.
